subject: High-resolution token sampling discrepancy — request for methodology and credit
messages:
From: Liam Chen <liam.chen@storify.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Finance Ops <billing@storify.ai>
Date: Sun, 26 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected 9/25 spike and sampling granularity question

Hi Soojin —

We spotted a ~42% spike in our 9/25 usage compared to daily baseline. The bill's "token sample" export (attached) shows a lot of high-cardinality short requests around 16:45–17:05 UTC. We use a high-resolution sampling job on our side for debug logging, but this level of short-lived sessions doesn't match our internal metrics.

Two quick asks:
- Can Redwood confirm whether the 9/25 ingest had a change in tokenization or sampling window that could cause short bursts to be double-counted?
- Can you provide the exact sampling methodology and binning window used for our account on that date (we need the per-minute aggregation logic and any session-merge heuristics)?

We attached a CSV export of the sample we pulled from your usage endpoint. We flagged rows where the model returned a 0-length user prompt but produced tokens on the assistant side — that looks like a tokenizer mismatch.

If this is a platform-side attribution issue, we'd like to know the credit path and timing for adjustments. We're close to month-end and need the reconciliation to close our books.

Thanks —
Liam
Liam Chen
Head of Platform — Storify AI
liam.chen@storify.ai
+1 (415) 555-0162

Attachment: usage-sample-export-20270925.csv (CSV, 24KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Liam Chen <liam.chen@storify.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected 9/25 spike and sampling granularity question

Hi Liam —

Thanks for the export and the clear examples — that's very helpful. I dug into the account's sampling pipeline and can confirm a couple of points off the bat:

- No configuration change was rolled to production on 9/25 that would alter tokenization or binning windows.
- We did deploy a performance patch to the batching scheduler on 9/24 evening (non-customer-facing) that changes micro-batching heuristics under very high concurrency; it should not alter token counts, but I want to rule out any side effects.

Ben / Rishi from Billing and Metering are looped here to provide the canonical per-minute aggregation used for billing and to run a comparative export. Rishi — can you pull the high-res ingest trace + the per-request tokenization matrix for Storify AI between 2027-09-25T16:30:00Z and 2027-09-25T17:10:00Z (UTC)? Please include request ids and the token attribution flag (user/assistant/system) and any session-id we used.

Action items from Redwood:
- Deliver the raw per-request lines (same format as Liam's attachment)
- Share our tokenization matrix PDF that shows model/tokenizer mapping used that day
- If we find platform-side attribution overcounting, propose a credit and timeline for application

I'll follow up by EOD PST with the requested exports or an interim update.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Liam Chen <liam.chen@storify.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected 9/25 spike and sampling granularity question

Hi all —

Attached are two things: 1) a high-resolution export (parity with your CSV columns) covering the requested window, and 2) our tokenization matrix for the specific model variant Storify was routed to on 9/25.

Preliminary notes after an initial pass:
- We see ~300 request-ids that match Liam's pattern where a request had an empty user prompt but assistant output tokens. Those align with short automated system probes from an internal partner dataset; they should have been marked as internal-test and not billed, but a routing label was missing on a subset due to a tag-propagation bug.
- The bug only affected requests routed through edge cluster eu-west-2 during a 16:40–16:52 UTC window because of a race in label replication.
- This explains why high-resolution sampling surfaces the issue more prominently than Storify's coarse counters. Your sample flagged precisely the same request-ids.

Next steps I propose:
- We will run a full scan for any requests in your account that were/should have been flagged internal-test and compute the overbilled token total.
- If confirmed, we will issue a pro-rated credit for the affected tokens and provide a corrected usage export.
- For tax/VAT handling: we will issue the credit on the next invoice cycle with an accounting memo. If Storify needs a retrospective VAT adjustment for EU entities, we can provide the breakdown and formal credit memo to feed into your tax filing process.

Ben — can you confirm the credit mechanics and expected timing once Rishi hands off the overcount total?

Regards,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Billing Systems Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Liam Chen <liam.chen@storify.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected 9/25 spike and sampling granularity question

Thanks Rishi — and Liam, sorry for the inconvenience. Quick note on process:

- Once Rishi provides the total token delta that should be credited, Redwood will generate an invoice credit reference (CR-<numeric>) and apply it to Storify's account the following billing run. Credits applied before invoice generation will reduce the upcoming invoice; credits applied after issuance will be refunded or applied as account credit per your preference.
- For amounts >$5k we issue a formal credit memo (PDF) that includes VAT treatment lines. Smaller credits appear as negative line items on the next invoice.
- Estimated timing: Rishi's audit + internal verification (~48 hours), credit issuance (~24 hours after verification). We aim to have the corrective credit visible on the 10/1 billing export.

Liam — can you confirm whether you prefer a direct refund to the payment method or a credit on account if we quantify the overbilling? Also, please confirm the entity to which VAT should be reconciled (Storify US entity vs Storify EU).

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Manager, Revenue Operations
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_tokenization-matrix.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Liam Chen <liam.chen@storify.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected 9/25 spike and sampling granularity question

Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick triage. Credit on account is fine for us (we close books manually and will apply it against October). For VAT: Storify is US-headquartered but we have EU sub-entity that reports VAT. Please include the VAT breakdown in the credit memo so our tax team can route it properly.

One small ask: can you add a short note in the export that marks which request-ids were "internal-test" versus production? That will make it very easy for us to crosswalk with our logs and confirm complete coverage.

If the total overbilled tokens is material, we'd like a brief postmortem summary of the label-propagation bug and the mitigation so we can present it to our procurement team.

Liam
